newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bond prices rise on unchanged Fed rates.
newsitem.headline: Danish bond prices rise on unchanged Fed rates.

text.p: Danish bond prices rose in early trade on Wednesday, tracking U.S. and German paper after Tuesday's Federal Reserve meeting left interest rates unchanged.
"The decision has been initially well received but there is still some uncertainty," a dealer said, adding that speculation of a rate rise would continue in the coming months.
At 0700 GMT the benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was up 0.32 point from Tuesday's close, at 111.24, yielding 6.29 percent.
The forthcoming benchmark seven percent state bond due 2007 rose 0.42 point, to 103.84, yielding 6.47 percent.
The yield gap between the 2006 bond and the German bund narrowed four basis points to 51 bp and the 2007-bund gap also narrowed by four bp, to 69.
The crown weakened to 3.8088 per mark from Tuesday's 3.8082.
